title: Canonical and unrestricted observations in a finite checkerboard gradient model
abstract: We compare canonical original-channel rectangle means with unrestricted linear observations for a finite two-channel source-weighted checkerboard gradient form. In dimensions 3 and 4 with orthogonal alternating weak lines, the minimum restoring unrestricted ranks are exactly Dn on all fields and (D-1)(n-2) on the actual real coexact domain. Complete diagonal-component means attain both ranks with normalized penalty c. At every fixed positive angle in any fixed dimension D>=3, an explicit transverse Fourier cutoff gives an unrestricted order-n count and a penalty independent of n, with angle-dependent constants. A real coexact cosine field defeats the mean-only extension at small positive angles. Canonical ambient rectangle restoration needs order n^(D-2) rows; in dimension 4 this matches a cited prior order-n^2 upper. The projection argument does not supply a coexact lower because rectangular averaging need not preserve that domain. A further actual coexact witness excludes partitions leaving a full coordinate in every cell of either channel. The three-dimensional canonical coexact linear-versus-logarithmic question remains open. Historical priority and practical relevance are unestablished; no physical Yang-Mills gap or continuum conclusion follows.
